key_insight: The quantum switch offers provable query advantages over definite-order circuits: exact simulation of general channels is impossible with finitely many calls in the worst case.
engineering_relevance: The switch can distinguish noise models with identical entanglement and average gate fidelities using dimension-independent device calls, suggesting value for noise characterization relevant to quantum error correction.
method: Compare coherent superpositions of operation orders with definite-order circuits allowing classical feed-forward and unlimited ancillary quantum memory.
Prove query lower bounds for exact simulation and approximation in half the diamond norm.
Analyze discrimination of fixed-unknown-basis dephasing from a theoretical depolarizing model.
evidence_signal: Theoretical bounds require Ω(d^{1/4}) circuit calls for any fixed simulation error below 1/2 and Ω(d^{1/16}) calls for the noise-discrimination task, versus dimension-independent switch use at fixed noise strength.
watch_item: These are theoretical query advantages; the abstract does not establish practical gains after switch implementation costs and experimental imperfections.
paper_title: Infinite or indefinite: the query cost of simulating the quantum switch
